title: Pillar Health - Latency & Capacity Planning
summary: Initial latency and capacity planning discovery for Pillar Health's patient-facing summarization service. Discussed p95 SLOs, concurrency targets, streaming vs batch, and validation benchmarks. Agreed to run a token/sec benchmark on Redwood hosted with a mirrored dataset and to evaluate a Dedicated pool if p95/SLO needs require it. Security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC) noted; Redwood to share security pack and pricing options.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack + SOC2 summary (Jordan)
Pillar to share 2 sample anonymized prompts and target load profile (Lina)
Schedule benchmark window: Redwood hosted token/sec run (Priya & Samir) - target week of Aug 18
Follow-up scoping call for Dedicated pool sizing if benchmarks exceed hosted costs (Jordan)
action_items: Jordan Hayes: Send security pack + pricing tier spreadsheet (due 2025-08-13)
Lina Park: Share anonymized prompt set and 95th percentile latency target details (due 2025-08-14)
Priya Kapoor: Run initial token/sec synthetic benchmark on hosted dev region and share results (due 2025-08-20)
Samir Kaur: Provide current traffic heatmap and max concurrent sessions (due 2025-08-15)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya my SE is here too. How's it going?
[00:10] Evan Morales: Good morning, Jordan. Evan here. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:15] Priya Kapoor: Hi team. Quick agenda — p95 targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, and then security constraints. We'll try not to overrun.
[00:28] Lina Park: Sounds great. We're trying to figure out if Redwood hosted will meet our latency SLOs for the patient summarization feature, or if we need Dedicated or Private.
[00:36] Jordan Hayes: Perfect. Can you give a bit of context on expected traffic shape? p95 target numbers?
[00:42] Lina Park: Sure. End users are doctors and nurses using a patient timeline with auto-summaries. Peak concurrency is about 600 concurrent sessions across region X, spiky during shift changes. p95 should be ~350ms for short summaries (~150 tokens), and under 800ms for longer ones (~600 tokens) — those are our ballpark SLOs.
[01:05] Samir Kaur: We care about streaming too — we want tokens to start flowing within 150ms for interactive feel. If initial token is slow, clinicians complain.
[01:15] Priya Kapoor: Ok, so two dimensions: p95 end-to-end generation latency, and streaming start latency. For hosted, we can often get good cold-warm behavior with prefix caching and small batch sizes; Dedicated gives you capacity guarantees for concurrent QPS.
[01:29] Evan Morales: Can you explain how Redwood determines the p95? Like does p95 include network + inference + SDK overhead?
[01:36] Priya Kapoor: Good question. Our p95 SLO numbers in docs typically reflect server-side inference time plus response streaming overhead from our edge. For a true end-to-end p95 you should add client-network RTT; we can instrument token-level timings and give you a breakdown per token, per-request. We'll share a sample trace.
[01:55] Jordan Hayes: Also worth noting model choice and quantization impact token/sec. Smaller quantized variants reduce latency but can introduce occasional quality delta. We'll flag that in recommendations.
[02:05] Lina Park: We're using an open model family similar to Llama2-ish; are there verifiable differences in p95 between 8-bit quant and FP16?
[02:12] Priya Kapoor: Yes. In our internal benchmarking 8-bit quant can reduce GPU memory and increase throughput but p95 for single-query latency can be slightly higher if kernels aren't fused for that path. For streaming with small sequence lengths (~150 tokens), FP16 on an optimized kernel often wins for p95. But if you need high tokens/sec for batch workloads, quant shines.
[02:40] Samir Kaur: Our priority is interactive tail latency. Cost is secondary but important. We may tolerate a 10-15% cost premium if p95 is solid.
[02:50] Jordan Hayes: That's helpful. For 600 concurrent sessions, assuming average tokens per request 200 with streaming, rough math — we should discuss batching policy. Do you expect many simultaneous small requests, or fewer larger ones?
[03:04] Lina Park: Mostly many small requests at shift changes, and periodic larger summary sweeps at night.
[03:12] Priya Kapoor: That profile maps well to hybrid routing: use a Dedicated pool for predictable daytime shift peaks if you want guaranteed p95, or hosted with autoscaling + fallback to a lower-cost model for non-critical loads. We can also do per-route SLOs.
[03:28] Evan Morales: How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching for repeat prompts? We have templates and a lot of similar contexts.
[03:35] Priya Kapoor: Our runtime supports KV cache reuse and prefix caching; that reduces per-token compute for repeated contexts. For templates you can pre-cache tokens server-side which dramatically reduces latency. We'll need to validate on your prompt set.
[03:50] Samir Kaur: Let's talk benchmarks — what would a token/sec benchmark look like from Redwood?
[03:58] Priya Kapoor: We'll run a benchmark in the hosted dev region simulating your concurrency and prompt distribution. We'll measure: 95th latency per request, initial token time (time to first byte), sustained tokens/sec per GPU, and total cost estimate. We usually run both streaming and non-streaming modes.
[04:20] Jordan Hayes: For Dedicated sizing we translate your 95th and concurrency targets into GPU pool size based on throughput curves. We'll give a few options: 1) small Dedicated pool sized for p95 350ms during peaks (higher cost), 2) hosted with burst capacity and smart routing (lower commit, slightly higher p95 risk).
[04:40] Lina Park: Any thoughts on regional fallbacks? We need data residency in region X, but can we overflow to region Y in emergencies?
[04:48] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we support strict region pinning for Private/Dedicated. Hosted can be configured to prefer region X and overflow to Y with customer approval; audit logs record overflows. Important: data residency rules could necessitate Private deployment.
[05:05] Evan Morales: Security checklist — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integrations for key management, and audit logs. Also, can logs be redacted before hitting Redwood?
[05:16] Jordan Hayes: We have a security pack including SOC2 report, SAML/SSO, KMS/HSM support, RBAC, and log export options. Redaction is possible at ingestion via customer-side preprocessing, or via our private connector in Private deployments. We'll send the pack.
[05:30] [00:05:30] Priya Kapoor: Quick aside: a lot of customers with 200-800 concurrent sessions opt for a small Dedicated pool for day-to-day and use hosted for burst — it gives predictable p95 without a huge commit.
[05:45] Lina Park: Pricing — ballpark difference between hosted and Dedicated? We need to justify to finance.
[05:50] Jordan Hayes: Ballpark: hosted is usage-based and predictable for low baseline usage; Dedicated is monthly commitment but reduces per-token price and provides throughput SLAs. We'll share a comparison grid.
[06:04] Samir Kaur: On the token/sec numbers — what's realistic on an A100-like device vs an H100-like device for our model family?
[06:12] Priya Kapoor: Roughly, for mid-sized models: A100 can do X tokens/sec (we'll provide numbers) and H100 improves throughput significantly, especially for long sequences due to better memory bandwidth. But the exact numbers depend on sequence length and kernel stack; we'll include a matrix in the benchmark report.
[06:33] Evan Morales: How much instrumentation do you provide? We want token-level traces and dashboarding for p50/p95/p99.
[06:40] Priya Kapoor: Redwood Console exposes token-level timelines, per-route p95/p99, and you can hook traces into your APM. We'll demo that on the follow-up.
[06:52] [00:06:52] Jordan Hayes: Let's capture assumptions for the benchmark: you will share 2 anonymized prompts (Lina), Samir will provide traffic heatmap, Redwood will run hosted synthetic test, and then we can interpret.
[07:02] Lina Park: One more nuance: we have HIPAA-adjacent data handling concerns. We may need Private with customer-managed keys if we move beyond prototype.
[07:12] Jordan Hayes: Understood. Private deployment options exist; we can show tradeoffs in the scoping doc.
[07:20] Evan Morales: What about warm/cold starts? Our users can't tolerate first-request spikes.
[07:26] Priya Kapoor: For hosted, warm pools and pre-warming can reduce cold-start tail. Dedicated avoids many of these issues since capacity is reserved; cold-starts are mostly during autoscaling events. We'll log pre-warm policies.
[07:40] Samir Kaur: Can you do canary rollouts with fallbacks? For model upgrades we want automatic fallback if p95 regresses.
[07:46] Jordan Hayes: Yes, rollouts with A/B and automatic rollback are supported. Redwood Optimize will surface regressions.
[07:54] [00:07:54] Evan Morales: Ok, what's a realistic timeline to validate hosted for our SLOs?
[08:00] Priya Kapoor: If you share prompts and heatmap by Aug 14, we can run hosted synthetic benchmarks by Aug 18 and deliver an initial report by Aug 20. Then decide whether Dedicated sizing is needed.
[08:13] Lina Park: That timeline works.
[08:16] Jordan Hayes: Great. A couple more technical things — for streaming, we measure time-to-first-token and sustained tokens/sec. If you need sub-150ms time-to-first-token, we'll likely recommend a Dedicated warm pool plus prefix caching for templates.
[08:30] Priya Kapoor: Also mention quantization: for worst-case p95 we may avoid aggressive quant if quality drops. We'll propose a quantization matrix with observed p95 deltas.
[08:40] Samir Kaur: What about client-side retries and backoff? Any best practices?
[08:44] Priya Kapoor: Exponential backoff and jitter is recommended. For interactive flows, keep client retry windows short and surface fallback messaging. We can provide recommended SDK configs.
[08:56] Evan Morales: Do you provide a benchmark corpus uploader or do we just send sample prompts?
[09:01] Jordan Hayes: For early-stage we take a sample set. For larger PoCs we can accept a flagged dataset in S3 or a secure upload. We'll need to anonymize PHI before transfer for HIPAA concerns.
[09:14] [00:09:14] Lina Park: Anything else around concurrency math? I want to ensure we're mapping p95 per-user vs p95 per-request correctly.
[09:21] Priya Kapoor: Usually SLOs are per-request p95. If you have multi-request user flows, we recommend a composite SLO and measuring end-to-end user-perceived latency. We'll help model the math for capacity planning.
[09:36] Samir Kaur: Could you share an example conversion: e.g., 600 concurrent sessions with avg 2 req/min => tokens/sec demand?
[09:44] Priya Kapoor: Sure. If 600 concurrent, 2 req/min = 20 req/s, times avg tokens per req 200 => 4k tokens/sec sustained. Add burst factor of 2. We'll run exact numbers in the benchmark.
[09:58] Jordan Hayes: Noted. We'll include headroom and safety margins.
[10:03] [00:10:03] Evan Morales: Okay let's talk deliverables so nothing slips: 1) security pack, 2) pricing grid hosted vs dedicated, 3) benchmark plan and target window, 4) sample traces.
[10:15] Jordan Hayes: We'll deliver those. Priya will run the hosted synthetic token/sec run and include token-level timing.
[10:22] Priya Kapoor: One small risk: for some prompt structures short-tail can be sensitive to decoding strategy—greedy vs sampling—so share your exact generation params.
[10:34] Lina Park: We'll export our generation params.
[10:38] Samir Kaur: Also, if we go to Private, what's the expected lift/engagement from Redwood for deployment?
[10:44] Jordan Hayes: For Private we provide an installer, operator runbook, and 2-week onboarding support. For air-gapped, additional engineering time is scheduled. We'll include that in the quote.
[10:56] [00:10:56] Evan Morales: Great. Any quick questions before we wrap?
[11:00] Lina Park: One last ask — can Redwood include a short NFR checklist for our procurement team?
[11:04] Jordan Hayes: Yes — we'll include an NFR one-pager in the security pack.
[11:08] Priya Kapoor: Ok, I'll start drafting the benchmark steps. Basic plan: synthetic load generator, 3 runs (low/med/high), measure time-to-first-token, sustained token/sec per GPU, and p95/p99 per request. We'll attach the raw CSV.
[11:25] Evan Morales: Sounds good.
[11:28] [00:11:28] Jordan Hayes: Recap: Redwood sends security pack + pricing, Pillar sends prompts and heatmap, Redwood runs hosted benchmark in dev region week of Aug 18, deliver report Aug 20, then scoping for Dedicated if needed.
[11:44] Lina Park: Thanks everyone, we'll get the artifacts to you.
[11:48] Samir Kaur: Thanks, talk soon.
[11:50] Jordan Hayes: Thanks all. Meeting adjourned.
[11:55] [END]
